chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Hasan ibn al-Zibrqan al-Ansari, who said: Is'haq al-Hadda' told me, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent for me while we were in Mina: 'Come to me, and with you are your tools.' So I went to him in his tent, greeted him, and he responded and gestured for me to sit. So I sat down. Then he took a new sandal and threw it to me. When I wanted to leave, I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! If you were to gift me this sandal, I could replicate it.' So he threw the other one to me and said, 'One? What benefit can it give you?' He said, 'And it was such that it has a support for the heel, narrow from its middle, and for it were two straps, and for it were heads. So he said: This is the footwear of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'.

key_terms.قِبَالَانِ: Two straps (typically across the top of the foot)
key_terms.كِنْفُكَ: Your tools or equipment (referring to the companion's trade)
key_terms.مُعَقَّبَةً: Having a heel support or strap that goes around the heel
key_terms.مِنْى: Mina, a location near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the sandal gifted by Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the concept of *tawathur* (consecutive transmission) in Shia scholarship, where material artifacts serve as tangible proofs of prophetic tradition (*Sunnah*). The Imam’s specific identification of the sandal’s design—described as *mu'abbah* (tied) and *mukhassarah* (shortened)—emphasizes the preservation of the Prophet’s physical appearance and customs (*sunan*) through direct lineage, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpreting religious practice.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Al Khazraj Al Hassan Bin Al Zabarqan Al Ansary, from Is’haq Al Haza’a who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> sent for me and we were at Mina: ‘Come to me<sup>asws</sup> and with you are your tools’. So I went over to him<sup>asws</sup> in his<sup>asws</sup> tent. I greeted him<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> responded to me, and gestured to me that I should be seated. So I sat down. Then he<sup>asws</sup> gave me a new sandal, and gave it at me. So when I wanted to go, I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup> ! If only you<sup>asws</sup> would gift these sandals to me, and I can replicate upon this’. So he<sup>asws</sup> gave with the other one, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One, which benefit can it give you?’ 
He (the narrator) said, ‘And it was such that it has a support for the heel, narrow from its middle, and for it were two straps, and for it were heads. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a shoe (footwear) of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from abu al-Khazraj al-Hassan ibn al-Zabarqan al-Ansariy who has said that narrated to me Ishaq al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, sent for me, when we were in Mina, to come to him with my tools. I went to his tent and offered him (the Imam) the greeting of peace to which he responded and made a hand gesture for me to sit down. I sat down. He (the Imam) took a new shoe and threw it to me. When I wanted to leave I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I wish you gave this sandal to me as a present so I can use it as a model. He (the Imam) threw the other pair to me saying, ‘How can you benefit from one pair?’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘It had a back support, a narrow middle part and two straps in their front part (to go between the toes). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the model of the footgear of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
